sanskrit: kad u̱ preṣṭā̍v i̱ṣāṁ ra̍yī̱ṇām a̍dhva̱ryantā̱ yad u̍nninī̱tho a̱pām | a̱yaṁ vā̍ṁ ya̱jño a̍kṛta̱ praśa̍sti̱ṁ vasu̍dhitī̱ avi̍tārā janānām ||
english: O most beloved, you who officiate as adhvaryus among wealth and treasure, when you lift the waters — this sacrifice has made your glory known, O you who hold riches, O guides of the people.

sanskrit: ā vā̱m aśvā̍sa̱ḥ śuca̍yaḥ paya̱spā vāta̍raṁhaso di̱vyāso̱ atyā̍ḥ | ma̱no̱juvo̱ vṛṣa̍ṇo vī̱tapṛ̍ṣṭhā̱ eha sva̱rājo̍ a̱śvinā̍ vahantu ||
english: May your bright, milk-drinking steeds, swift as the wind, those heavenly coursers with backs unsaddled — thought-swift, vigorous bulls — bearing heavenly sovereignty, bring you Aśvins hither.

sanskrit: ā vā̱ṁ ratho̱ 'vani̱r na pra̱vatvā̍n sṛ̱prava̍ndhuraḥ suvi̱tāya̍ gamyāḥ | vṛṣṇa̍ḥ sthātārā̱ mana̍so̱ javī̍yān ahampū̱rvo ya̍ja̱to dhi̍ṣṇyā̱ yaḥ ||
english: May your chariot, like a rushing river, with a yoke that glides forward, come hither for our welfare. It is swifter than thought, carrying the vigorous bull — that adorable, zealous one who presses forward first.

sanskrit: i̱heha̍ jā̱tā sam a̍vāvaśītām are̱pasā̍ ta̱nvā̱3̱̍ nāma̍bhi̱ḥ svaiḥ | ji̱ṣṇur vā̍m a̱nyaḥ suma̍khasya sū̱rir di̱vo a̱nyaḥ su̱bhaga̍ḥ pu̱tra ū̍he ||
english: Born here and there, both have called out together with sinless body and with their own names. One of you is the conquering hero, patron of the bountiful sacrifice; the other, fortunate son of heaven, is glorified in the chariot race.

sanskrit: pra vā̍ṁ nice̱ruḥ ka̍ku̱ho vaśā̱m̐ anu̍ pi̱śaṅga̍rūpa̱ḥ sada̍nāni gamyāḥ | harī̍ a̱nyasya̍ pī̱paya̍nta̱ vājai̍r ma̱thrā rajā̍ṁsy aśvinā̱ vi ghoṣai̍ḥ ||
english: Your Kakuha mare, tawny in hue, has gone forward following the steeds to your dwelling-places. The bay horses of one of you are fattened with prizes; the sky-regions resound, O Aśvins, with your songs of victory.

sanskrit: pra vā̍ṁ śa̱radvā̍n vṛṣa̱bho na ni̱ṣṣāṭ pū̱rvīr iṣa̍ś carati̱ madhva̍ i̱ṣṇan | evai̍r a̱nyasya̍ pī̱paya̍nta̱ vājai̱r veṣa̍ntīr ū̱rdhvā na̱dyo̍ na̱ āgu̍ḥ ||
english: Like a vigorous bull in autumn, your chariot has sped forth, seeking refreshment, traversing many food-offerings laden with honey. With like prizes the streams have come to us like rivers flowing upward, fattening the other.

sanskrit: asa̍rji vā̱ṁ sthavi̍rā vedhasā̱ gīr bā̱ḻhe a̍śvinā tre̱dhā kṣara̍ntī | upa̍stutāv avata̱ṁ nādha̍māna̱ṁ yāma̱nn ayā̍mañ chṛṇuta̱ṁ hava̍m me ||
english: A firm and wise hymn has been sent forth to you, O Aśvins, flowing in three streams through the sacrifice. O you who are praised, protect the supplicant — whether in the course of the journey or at rest, hear my call.

sanskrit: u̱ta syā vā̱ṁ ruśa̍to̱ vapsa̍so̱ gīs tri̍ba̱rhiṣi̱ sada̍si pinvate̱ nṝn | vṛṣā̍ vām me̱gho vṛ̍ṣaṇā pīpāya̱ gor na seke̱ manu̍ṣo daśa̱syan ||
english: Moreover, that bright, radiant hymn of yours fills men at the triple sacrificial seat. The rain-cloud, O vigorous ones, has swelled for you both, like a cow's milk, pouring forth for the worshipper of Manu.

sanskrit: yu̱vām pū̱ṣevā̍śvinā̱ pura̍ṁdhir a̱gnim u̱ṣāṁ na ja̍rate ha̱viṣmā̍n | hu̱ve yad vā̍ṁ variva̱syā gṛ̍ṇā̱no vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: The full-purposed worshipper praises you two, O Aśvins, like Pūṣan, like Agni at the dawns, bearing oblations. As I call to you, singing your praises, seeking wide space — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: abhū̍d i̱daṁ va̱yuna̱m o ṣu bhū̍ṣatā̱ ratho̱ vṛṣa̍ṇvā̱n mada̍tā manīṣiṇaḥ | dhi̱ya̱ṁji̱nvā dhiṣṇyā̍ vi̱śpalā̍vasū di̱vo napā̍tā su̱kṛte̱ śuci̍vratā ||
english: This course has now appeared — come, O wise ones, adorn the vigorous chariot, rejoice! O you who impel thought, you who are zealous, who possess the riches of Viśpalā, O sons of heaven — you of good deeds and pure vows.

sanskrit: indra̍tamā̱ hi dhiṣṇyā̍ ma̱rutta̍mā da̱srā daṁsi̍ṣṭhā ra̱thyā̍ ra̱thīta̍mā | pū̱rṇaṁ ratha̍ṁ vahethe̱ madhva̱ āci̍ta̱ṁ tena̍ dā̱śvāṁsa̱m upa̍ yātho aśvinā ||
english: For you are the most Indra-like, the most zealous, the most Marut-like, O wonder-workers, the most skilled in deeds, the best of charioteers. You drive a chariot laden full of honey; with that chariot, O Aśvins, come to the worshipper.

sanskrit: kim atra̍ dasrā kṛṇutha̱ḥ kim ā̍sāthe̱ jano̱ yaḥ kaś ci̱d aha̍vir mahī̱yate̍ | ati̍ kramiṣṭaṁ ju̱rata̍m pa̱ṇer asu̱ṁ jyoti̱r viprā̍ya kṛṇutaṁ vaca̱syave̍ ||
english: What do you do here, O wonder-workers? What person who offers no oblations is glorified in your presence? You shall pass beyond the niggard Paṇi; restore the life-breath to the sage, and make light for the eloquent singer.

sanskrit: ja̱mbhaya̍tam a̱bhito̱ rāya̍ta̱ḥ śuno̍ ha̱tam mṛdho̍ vi̱dathu̱s tāny a̍śvinā | vāca̍ṁ-vācaṁ jari̱tū ra̱tninī̍ṁ kṛtam u̱bhā śaṁsa̍ṁ nāsatyāvata̱m mama̍ ||
english: Crush on all sides the hounds that bark and snap; strike them down, O Aśvins — you have discovered those things. Make every hymn of the praiser yield riches; both of you, O Nāsatyas, uphold my praise.

sanskrit: yu̱vam e̱taṁ ca̍krathu̱ḥ sindhu̍ṣu pla̱vam ā̍tma̱nvanta̍m pa̱kṣiṇa̍ṁ tau̱gryāya̱ kam | yena̍ deva̱trā mana̍sā nirū̱hathu̍ḥ supapta̱nī pe̍tathu̱ḥ kṣoda̍so ma̱haḥ ||
english: You made a raft for Tugra's son upon the rivers — a self-propelled raft with wings. With that raft, guided by divine thought, you flew well, soaring over the great waves.

sanskrit: ava̍viddhaṁ tau̱gryam a̱psv a1̱̍ntar a̍nārambha̱ṇe tama̍si̱ pravi̍ddham | cata̍sro̱ nāvo̱ jaṭha̍lasya̱ juṣṭā̱ ud a̱śvibhyā̍m iṣi̱tāḥ pā̍rayanti ||
english: The son of Tugra had been cast down into the waters, cast into darkness that offers no foothold. Four ships favored by Jaṭhala, driven by the Aśvins, carried him across.

sanskrit: kaḥ svi̍d vṛ̱kṣo niṣṭhi̍to̱ madhye̱ arṇa̍so̱ yaṁ tau̱gryo nā̍dhi̱taḥ pa̱ryaṣa̍svajat | pa̱rṇā mṛ̱gasya̍ pa̱taro̍r ivā̱rabha̱ ud a̍śvinā ūhathu̱ḥ śroma̍tāya̱ kam ||
english: What tree stood firm in the midst of the ocean, to which Taugra's son clung without hold? Just as the feathers of a flying bird, the Aśvins carried him upward — to Bhujyu for his glory.

sanskrit: tad vā̍ṁ narā nāsatyā̱v anu̍ ṣyā̱d yad vā̱m mānā̍sa u̱catha̱m avo̍can | a̱smād a̱dya sada̍saḥ so̱myād ā vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: May that, O heroes, O Nāsatyas, follow you — what the sages of inspired mind have uttered in praise of you. From this soma-session today, may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: taṁ yu̍ñjāthā̱m mana̍so̱ yo javī̍yān trivandhu̱ro vṛ̍ṣaṇā̱ yas tri̍ca̱kraḥ | yeno̍payā̱thaḥ su̱kṛto̍ duro̱ṇaṁ tri̱dhātu̍nā patatho̱ vir na pa̱rṇaiḥ ||
english: Harness that steed which is swifter than thought — the three-felied, three-wheeled chariot of the vigorous pair — by which you come near to the house of the good man; you fly with the three-fold element, like a bird with wings.

sanskrit: su̱vṛd ratho̍ vartate̱ yann a̱bhi kṣāṁ yat tiṣṭha̍tha̱ḥ kratu̍ma̱ntānu̍ pṛ̱kṣe | vapu̍r vapu̱ṣyā sa̍catām i̱yaṁ gīr di̱vo du̍hi̱troṣasā̍ sacethe ||
english: Your well-wheeled chariot rolls on toward the earth; when you stand, O wise ones, at the refreshments offered — let beauty attend beauty: may this hymn be with you, and may you Aśvins accompany Uṣas, the daughter of heaven.

sanskrit: ā ti̍ṣṭhataṁ su̱vṛta̱ṁ yo ratho̍ vā̱m anu̍ vra̱tāni̱ varta̍te ha̱viṣmā̍n | yena̍ narā nāsatyeṣa̱yadhyai̍ va̱rtir yā̱thas tana̍yāya̱ tmane̍ ca ||
english: Mount the well-wheeled chariot that rolls according to your ordinances, that bears the oblation. By which, O heroes, O Nāsatyas, you travel the path for nourishment, for offspring, and for the soul's own sake.

sanskrit: mā vā̱ṁ vṛko̱ mā vṛ̱kīr ā da̍dharṣī̱n mā pari̍ varktam u̱ta māti̍ dhaktam | a̱yaṁ vā̍m bhā̱go nihi̍ta i̱yaṁ gīr dasrā̍v i̱me vā̍ṁ ni̱dhayo̱ madhū̍nām ||
english: May neither wolf nor she-wolf attack you; do not turn away from us, and do not abandon us. This is the share laid up for you; this is the hymn, O wonder-workers — these are the honey-filled treasures deposited for you.

sanskrit: yu̱vāṁ gota̍maḥ purumī̱ḻho atri̱r dasrā̱ hava̱te 'va̍se ha̱viṣmā̍n | diśa̱ṁ na di̱ṣṭām ṛ̍jū̱yeva̱ yantā me̱ hava̍ṁ nāsa̱tyopa̍ yātam ||
english: Gotama, Purumīḷha, Atri — the oblation-bearer calls on you two, O wonder-workers, for help. Like one going straight toward a pointed direction, come near to my call, O Nāsatyas.

sanskrit: atā̍riṣma̱ tama̍sas pā̱ram a̱sya prati̍ vā̱ṁ stomo̍ aśvināv adhāyi | eha yā̍tam pa̱thibhi̍r deva̱yānai̍r vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: We have crossed to the far shore of this darkness; the hymn of praise has been established for you, O Aśvins. Come here by the god-travelled paths — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: tā vā̍m a̱dya tāv a̍pa̱raṁ hu̍vemo̱cchantyā̍m u̱ṣasi̱ vahni̍r u̱kthaiḥ | nāsa̍tyā̱ kuha̍ ci̱t santā̍v a̱ryo di̱vo napā̍tā su̱dāsta̍rāya ||
english: I, the carrier, invoke you both today and again at the dawning of Uṣas with praises. O Nāsatyas, wherever you may be, O noble sons of heaven, come to the generous giver.

sanskrit: a̱sme ū̱ ṣu vṛ̍ṣaṇā mādayethā̱m ut pa̱ṇīm̐r ha̍tam ū̱rmyā mada̍ntā | śru̱tam me̱ accho̍ktibhir matī̱nām eṣṭā̍ narā̱ nice̍tārā ca̱ karṇai̍ḥ ||
english: O vigorous pair, do rejoice among us; strike down the stingy Paṇis in your exhilaration. Be heard by me — O heroes, discerning ones, be sought out with the ear through the utterances of my thoughts.

sanskrit: śri̱ye pū̍ṣann iṣu̱kṛte̍va de̱vā nāsa̍tyā vaha̱tuṁ sū̱ryāyā̍ḥ | va̱cyante̍ vāṁ kaku̱hā a̱psu jā̱tā yu̱gā jū̱rṇeva̱ varu̍ṇasya̱ bhūre̍ḥ ||
english: For glory, like Pūṣan and the arrow-maker among the gods, O Nāsatyas, bring the marriage of Sūryā. Your Kakuha mare, born of the waters, is celebrated — like the ancient yokes of mighty Varuṇa.

sanskrit: a̱sme sā vā̍m mādhvī rā̱tir a̍stu̱ stoma̍ṁ hinotam mā̱nyasya̍ kā̱roḥ | anu̱ yad vā̍ṁ śrava̱syā̍ sudānū su̱vīryā̍ya carṣa̱ṇayo̱ mada̍nti ||
english: May that sweet gift of yours be for us; impel the hymn of the praiser who deserves honor. While the peoples rejoice, O munificent ones renowned in glory, may they rejoice in heroic strength through you.

sanskrit: e̱ṣa vā̱ṁ stomo̍ aśvināv akāri̱ māne̍bhir maghavānā suvṛ̱kti | yā̱taṁ va̱rtis tana̍yāya̱ tmane̍ cā̱gastye̍ nāsatyā̱ mada̍ntā ||
english: This hymn has been made for you, O Aśvins, O bountiful ones, with songs of praise and well-wrought verses. Come, rejoicing, O Nāsatyas, to the path for offspring and for the self — for Agastya's sake.

sanskrit: atā̍riṣma̱ tama̍sas pā̱ram a̱sya prati̍ vā̱ṁ stomo̍ aśvināv adhāyi | eha yā̍tam pa̱thibhi̍r deva̱yānai̍r vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: We have crossed to the far shore of this darkness; the hymn of praise has been established for you, O Aśvins. Come here by the god-travelled paths — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: ka̱ta̱rā pūrvā̍ kata̱rāpa̍rā̱yoḥ ka̱thā jā̱te ka̍vaya̱ḥ ko vi ve̍da | viśva̱ṁ tmanā̍ bibhṛto̱ yad dha̱ nāma̱ vi va̍rtete̱ aha̍nī ca̱kriye̍va ||
english: Which of the two is the earlier and which the later of these two? How were they born? Who among the wise truly knows? They bear all of creation within themselves by name; the two days revolve like wheels.

sanskrit: bhūri̱ṁ dve aca̍rantī̱ cara̍ntam pa̱dvanta̱ṁ garbha̍m a̱padī̍ dadhāte | nitya̱ṁ na sū̱num pi̱tror u̱pasthe̱ dyāvā̱ rakṣa̍tam pṛthivī no̱ abhvā̍t ||
english: The two ever-moving ones carry the many and support the moving — the footed embryo held by the footless. Like a son forever in the lap of his parents — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: a̱ne̱ho dā̱tram adi̍ter ana̱rvaṁ hu̱ve sva̍rvad ava̱dhaṁ nama̍svat | tad ro̍dasī janayataṁ jari̱tre dyāvā̱ rakṣa̍tam pṛthivī no̱ abhvā̍t ||
english: I invoke the faultless, unopposed gift of Aditi, radiant and inexhaustible, worthy of reverence. May both the great ones engender that for the singer — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: ata̍pyamāne̱ ava̱sāva̍ntī̱ anu̍ ṣyāma̱ roda̍sī de̱vapu̍tre | u̱bhe de̱vānā̍m u̱bhaye̍bhi̱r ahnā̱ṁ dyāvā̱ rakṣa̍tam pṛthivī no̱ abhvā̍t ||
english: May we be near the two divine daughters, the pair of worlds that are heated without distress, filled with refreshment. Both belong to the gods, both on both types of days — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: sa̱ṁgaccha̍māne yuva̱tī sama̍nte̱ svasā̍rā jā̱mī pi̱tror u̱pasthe̍ | a̱bhi̱jighra̍ntī̱ bhuva̍nasya̱ nābhi̱ṁ dyāvā̱ rakṣa̍tam pṛthivī no̱ abhvā̍t ||
english: The two young women, sisters and kindred, come together, meeting in the lap of their father; sniffing toward the navel of the world — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: u̱rvī sadma̍nī bṛha̱tī ṛ̱tena̍ hu̱ve de̱vānā̱m ava̍sā̱ jani̍trī | da̱dhāte̱ ye a̱mṛta̍ṁ su̱pratī̍ke̱ dyāvā̱ rakṣa̍tam pṛthivī no̱ abhvā̍t ||
english: I invoke the two vast, great, ordinance-firm dwelling-places, mothers of the gods, for their divine aid. They who sustain the immortal in good aspect — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: u̱rvī pṛ̱thvī ba̍hu̱le dū̱rea̍nte̱ upa̍ bruve̱ nama̍sā ya̱jñe a̱smin | da̱dhāte̱ ye su̱bhage̍ su̱pratū̍rtī̱ dyāvā̱ rakṣa̍tam pṛthivī no̱ abhvā̍t ||
english: The wide and broad, the many-folded ones with distant ends — I address them with reverence at this sacrifice. They who sustain good fortune, who are easy to approach — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: de̱vān vā̱ yac ca̍kṛ̱mā kac ci̱d āga̱ḥ sakhā̍yaṁ vā̱ sada̱m ij jāspa̍tiṁ vā | i̱yaṁ dhīr bhū̍yā ava̱yāna̍m eṣā̱ṁ dyāvā̱ rakṣa̍tam pṛthivī no̱ abhvā̍t ||
english: Whatever sin we have committed against the gods, against a comrade or against the house-lord ever-faithful — may this prayer of ours be the atonement for them. O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

sanskrit: u̱bhā śaṁsā̱ naryā̱ mām a̍viṣṭām u̱bhe mām ū̱tī ava̍sā sacetām | bhūri̍ cid a̱ryaḥ su̱dāsta̍rāye̱ṣā mada̍nta iṣayema devāḥ ||
english: May both manly praises strengthen me; may both accompany me with protection and support. Among many a noble lord, may the gods rejoice in the liberal giver — and may we press forward with vigor, O gods.

sanskrit: ṛ̱taṁ di̱ve tad a̍vocam pṛthi̱vyā a̍bhiśrā̱vāya̍ pratha̱maṁ su̍me̱dhāḥ | pā̱tām a̍va̱dyād du̍ri̱tād a̱bhīke̍ pi̱tā mā̱tā ca̍ rakṣatā̱m avo̍bhiḥ ||
english: I, of good understanding, spoke to Heaven and Earth first, so that they might hear this truth. May father and mother protect us from blame and from ill-going near at hand, with their aids.

sanskrit: i̱daṁ dyā̍vāpṛthivī sa̱tyam a̍stu̱ pita̱r māta̱r yad i̱hopa̍bru̱ve vā̍m | bhū̱taṁ de̱vānā̍m ava̱me avo̍bhir vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: O Heaven and Earth, O Father and Mother — may what I address to you here be true. May we be foremost among the gods with their aids — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: ā na̱ iḻā̍bhir vi̱dathe̍ suśa̱sti vi̱śvāna̍raḥ savi̱tā de̱va e̍tu | api̱ yathā̍ yuvāno̱ matsa̍thā no̱ viśva̱ṁ jaga̍d abhipi̱tve ma̍nī̱ṣā ||
english: Let divine Savitṛ, the universal lord, come to us at the festival with praises and fine speech, so that you, O youthful ones, may delight in us with inspired thought at the gathering of all the world.

sanskrit: ā no̱ viśva̱ āskrā̍ gamantu de̱vā mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā varu̍ṇaḥ sa̱joṣā̍ḥ | bhuva̱n yathā̍ no̱ viśve̍ vṛ̱dhāsa̱ḥ kara̍n su̱ṣāhā̍ vithu̱raṁ na śava̍ḥ ||
english: May all the gods come to us with all the horses — Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa together in accord, so that all may prosper us, making us triumphant over the unstable one, like strength.

sanskrit: preṣṭha̍ṁ vo̱ ati̍thiṁ gṛṇīṣe̱ 'gniṁ śa̱stibhi̍s tu̱rvaṇi̍ḥ sa̱joṣā̍ḥ | asa̱d yathā̍ no̱ varu̍ṇaḥ sukī̱rtir iṣa̍ś ca parṣad arigū̱rtaḥ sū̱riḥ ||
english: Together with Turvaṇi I praise Agni, your dearest guest, with hymns. May glorious Varuṇa be ours, and may the patron, praised of foes, conduct us to refreshments.

sanskrit: upa̍ va̱ eṣe̱ nama̍sā jigī̱ṣoṣāsā̱naktā̍ su̱dughe̍va dhe̱nuḥ | sa̱mā̱ne aha̍n vi̱mimā̍no a̱rkaṁ viṣu̍rūpe̱ paya̍si̱ sasmi̱nn ūdha̍n ||
english: I come near to them both with reverence, desiring conquest — Dawn and Night, like an easily milked cow. On the same day I measure out the hymn, the milk flowing from their one udder in different forms.

sanskrit: u̱ta no 'hi̍r bu̱dhnyo̱3̱̍ maya̍s ka̱ḥ śiśu̱ṁ na pi̱pyuṣī̍va veti̱ sindhu̍ḥ | yena̱ napā̍tam a̱pāṁ ju̱nāma̍ mano̱juvo̱ vṛṣa̍ṇo̱ yaṁ vaha̍nti ||
english: May Ahir Budhnya bring us joy, and may the river Sindhu come like a suckling nursing her young — the river by which we impel the offspring of the waters, the vigorous steed, swift as thought, whom they carry.

sanskrit: u̱ta na̍ ī̱ṁ tvaṣṭā ga̱ntv acchā̱ smat sū̱ribhi̍r abhipi̱tve sa̱joṣā̍ḥ | ā vṛ̍tra̱hendra̍ś carṣaṇi̱prās tu̱viṣṭa̍mo na̱rāṁ na̍ i̱ha ga̍myāḥ ||
english: May Tvaṣṭṛ too come toward us together with the patrons at the gathering, united in purpose. May Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, who fills all peoples, the most mighty of men, come to us here.

sanskrit: u̱ta na̍ īm ma̱tayo 'śva̍yogā̱ḥ śiśu̱ṁ na gāva̱s taru̍ṇaṁ rihanti | tam ī̱ṁ giro̱ jana̍yo̱ na patnī̍ḥ sura̱bhiṣṭa̍maṁ na̱rāṁ na̍santa ||
english: Also our thoughts, harnessed like horses, lick the young one like cows licking a calf. Hymns praise him as wives praise their husband — him, the most fragrant among men.

sanskrit: u̱ta na̍ īm ma̱ruto̍ vṛ̱ddhase̍nā̱ḥ smad roda̍sī̱ sama̍nasaḥ sadantu | pṛṣa̍daśvāso̱ 'vana̍yo̱ na rathā̍ ri̱śāda̍so mitra̱yujo̱ na de̱vāḥ ||
english: May the Maruts too, with swelling armies, together with the two worlds, sit down among us in one accord — they whose steeds are dappled, rolling like rivers, consuming enemies, yoked as with Mitra, like gods.

sanskrit: pra nu yad e̍ṣām mahi̱nā ci̍ki̱tre pra yu̍ñjate pra̱yuja̱s te su̍vṛ̱kti | adha̱ yad e̍ṣāṁ su̱dine̱ na śaru̱r viśva̱m eri̍ṇam pruṣā̱yanta̱ senā̍ḥ ||
english: Truly now their greatness shines forth; the draft animals are harnessed with excellent harnessing. And when on a fair day their armies scatter the arrow of destruction, they sprinkle all the desert.

sanskrit: pro a̱śvinā̱v ava̍se kṛṇudhva̱m pra pū̱ṣaṇa̱ṁ svata̍vaso̱ hi santi̍ | a̱dve̱ṣo viṣṇu̱r vāta̍ ṛbhu̱kṣā acchā̍ su̱mnāya̍ vavṛtīya de̱vān ||
english: Send forth the Aśvins for protection; send forth Pūṣan — for they are truly self-strong. May I turn to the gods — non-hostile Viṣṇu, Vāta, Ṛbhukṣan — seeking their benevolence.

sanskrit: i̱yaṁ sā vo̍ a̱sme dīdhi̍tir yajatrā api̱prāṇī̍ ca̱ sada̍nī ca bhūyāḥ | ni yā de̱veṣu̱ yata̍te vasū̱yur vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: May this thought of ours for you, O adorable ones, be life-giving and settled among you — this thought of one who strives after wealth among the gods. May we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: pi̱tuṁ nu sto̍ṣam ma̱ho dha̱rmāṇa̱ṁ tavi̍ṣīm | yasya̍ tri̱to vy oja̍sā vṛ̱traṁ vipa̍rvam a̱rdaya̍t ||
english: Now I shall praise the food — great, law-sustaining, vigorous — by whose strength Trita crushed the many-jointed Vṛtra with force.

sanskrit: svādo̍ pito̱ madho̍ pito va̱yaṁ tvā̍ vavṛmahe | a̱smāka̍m avi̱tā bha̍va ||
english: O sweet food, O honeyed food — we have chosen you. Be our protector.

sanskrit: upa̍ naḥ pita̱v ā ca̍ra śi̱vaḥ śi̱vābhi̍r ū̱tibhi̍ḥ | ma̱yo̱bhur a̍dviṣe̱ṇyaḥ sakhā̍ su̱śevo̱ adva̍yāḥ ||
english: Come to us, O food; approach with auspicious aids, bringing bliss. Be a friend free of hatred, charming, without duplicity.

sanskrit: tava̱ tye pi̍to̱ rasā̱ rajā̱ṁsy anu̱ viṣṭhi̍tāḥ | di̱vi vātā̍ iva śri̱tāḥ ||
english: Your savors, O food, are spread out through the realms, resting there like winds in the sky.

sanskrit: tava̱ tye pi̍to̱ dada̍ta̱s tava̍ svādiṣṭha̱ te pi̍to | pra svā̱dmāno̱ rasā̍nāṁ tuvi̱grīvā̍ iverate ||
english: Yours, O food, are they who give; yours, O food, is the sweetest. The savors, swelling in taste, surge forward like those with great necks.

sanskrit: tve pi̍to ma̱hānā̍ṁ de̱vānā̱m mano̍ hi̱tam | akā̍ri̱ cāru̍ ke̱tunā̱ tavāhi̍m ava̍sāvadhīt ||
english: In you, O food, the mind of the great gods is established. With your lovely banner, one has slain Ahi with your aid.

sanskrit: yad a̱do pi̍to̱ aja̍gan vi̱vasva̱ parva̍tānām | atrā̍ cin no madho pi̱to 'ra̍m bha̱kṣāya̍ gamyāḥ ||
english: When you, O food, went to the Vivasvat of the mountains, even there, O sweet food, come to us sufficiently for nourishment.

sanskrit: yad a̱pām oṣa̍dhīnām pari̱ṁśam ā̍ri̱śāma̍he | vātā̍pe̱ pīva̱ id bha̍va ||
english: When we partake of the essence of the waters and plants, O Vātāpe, become fat indeed.

sanskrit: yat te̍ soma̱ gavā̍śiro̱ yavā̍śiro̱ bhajā̍mahe | vātā̍pe̱ pīva̱ id bha̍va ||
english: When we partake of you, O Soma, whether mixed with milk or mixed with barley, O Vātāpe, become fat indeed.

sanskrit: ka̱ra̱mbha o̍ṣadhe bhava̱ pīvo̍ vṛ̱kka u̍dāra̱thiḥ | vātā̍pe̱ pīva̱ id bha̍va ||
english: Be porridge, O herb; be fat in the kidneys of the charioteer. O Vātāpe, become fat indeed.

sanskrit: taṁ tvā̍ va̱yam pi̍to̱ vaco̍bhi̱r gāvo̱ na ha̱vyā su̍ṣūdima | de̱vebhya̍s tvā sadha̱māda̍m a̱smabhya̍ṁ tvā sadha̱māda̍m ||
english: You, O food, we have refined with our words, as cows press out what is to be offered. For the gods you are a shared feast; for us too you are a shared feast.

sanskrit: sami̍ddho a̱dya rā̍jasi de̱vo de̱vaiḥ sa̍hasrajit | dū̱to ha̱vyā ka̍vir va̍ha ||
english: Kindled today you reign as god among the gods, winning thousands. O Agni, wise seer and messenger, carry the oblations.

sanskrit: tanū̍napād ṛ̱taṁ ya̱te madhvā̍ ya̱jñaḥ sam a̍jyate | dadha̍t saha̱sriṇī̱r iṣa̍ḥ ||
english: By Tanūnapāt, the sacrifice is anointed with honey as the truth-seeker proceeds; he bestows thousandfold refreshments.

sanskrit: ā̱juhvā̍no na̱ īḍyo̍ de̱vām̐ ā va̍kṣi ya̱jñiyā̍n | agne̍ sahasra̱sā a̍si ||
english: You who are praised and worthy of hymns, being invoked, bring the worshipful gods hither. O Agni, you are the winner of thousands.

sanskrit: prā̱cīna̍m ba̱rhir oja̍sā sa̱hasra̍vīram astṛṇan | yatrā̍dityā vi̱rāja̍tha ||
english: With might they have strewn the eastward-facing sacred grass, that has a thousand heroes — there where the Ādityas reign.

sanskrit: vi̱rāṭ sa̱mrāḍ vi̱bhvīḥ pra̱bhvīr ba̱hvīś ca̱ bhūya̍sīś ca̱ yāḥ | duro̍ ghṛ̱tāny a̍kṣaran ||
english: She who is the virāj, she who is the samrāj, the pervasive and the powerful, the many and the yet more numerous — from the doors the streams of ghee have flowed.

sanskrit: su̱ru̱kme hi su̱peśa̱sādhi̍ śri̱yā vi̱rāja̍taḥ | u̱ṣāsā̱v eha sī̍datām ||
english: Well-decked and well-adorned, they two shine in beauty. May the two Dawns sit down here.

sanskrit: pra̱tha̱mā hi su̱vāca̍sā̱ hotā̍rā̱ daivyā̍ ka̱vī | ya̱jñaṁ no̍ yakṣatām i̱mam ||
english: For the first two are the divine priestly callers, the poets of fair speech. May they sacrifice this sacrifice of ours.

sanskrit: bhāra̱tīḻe̍ sara̱svatī̱ yā va̱ḥ sarvā̍ upabru̱ve | tā na̍ś codayata śri̱ye ||
english: Bhāratī, Iḷā, and Sarasvatī — all of you I address here. May those three spur us on to glory.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā̍ rū̱pāṇi̱ hi pra̱bhuḥ pa̱śūn viśvā̍n samāna̱je | teṣā̍ṁ naḥ sphā̱tim ā ya̍ja ||
english: For Tvaṣṭṛ is the lord of all forms; he has assembled all cattle. Sacrifice their increase for us.

sanskrit: upa̱ tmanyā̍ vanaspate̱ pātho̍ de̱vebhya̍ḥ sṛja | a̱gnir ha̱vyāni̍ siṣvadat ||
english: O Vanaspati, release the offering silently for the gods. Let Agni taste the oblations.

sanskrit: pu̱ro̱gā a̱gnir de̱vānā̍ṁ gāya̱treṇa̱ sam a̍jyate | svāhā̍kṛtīṣu rocate ||
english: Agni goes before the gods and is anointed with the Gāyatrī metre; he shines bright in the svāhā oblations.

sanskrit: agne̱ naya̍ su̱pathā̍ rā̱ye a̱smān viśvā̍ni deva va̱yunā̍ni vi̱dvān | yu̱yo̱dhy a1̱̍smaj ju̍hurā̱ṇam eno̱ bhūyi̍ṣṭhāṁ te̱ nama̍-uktiṁ vidhema ||
english: O Agni, lead us by the good path to wealth, O god who knows all the ways. Ward off from us the sin that lurks and misleads — we would render to you the most frequent utterance of homage.

sanskrit: agne̱ tvam pā̍rayā̱ navyo̍ a̱smān sva̱stibhi̱r ati̍ du̱rgāṇi̱ viśvā̍ | pūś ca̍ pṛ̱thvī ba̍hu̱lā na̍ u̱rvī bhavā̍ to̱kāya̱ tana̍yāya̱ śaṁ yoḥ ||
english: O Agni, as one renewed, carry us across all difficulties with well-being; and the wide, broad earth be for us spacious. Be a source of peace and healing for our children and our progeny.

sanskrit: agne̱ tvam a̱smad yu̍yo̱dhy amī̍vā̱ ana̍gnitrā a̱bhy a̍manta kṛ̱ṣṭīḥ | puna̍r a̱smabhya̍ṁ suvi̱tāya̍ deva̱ kṣāṁ viśve̍bhir a̱mṛte̍bhir yajatra ||
english: O Agni, ward off from us the disease; peoples without fire have afflicted us. O god, O adorable one, restore the earth to us for well-being together with all the immortals.

sanskrit: pā̱hi no̍ agne pā̱yubhi̱r aja̍srair u̱ta pri̱ye sada̍na̱ ā śu̍śu̱kvān | mā te̍ bha̱yaṁ ja̍ri̱tāra̍ṁ yaviṣṭha nū̱naṁ vi̍da̱n māpa̱raṁ sa̍hasvaḥ ||
english: Protect us, O Agni, with unceasing guards; and shining bright in the beloved home — may your praiser know no fear now or in future, O youngest and most powerful.

sanskrit: mā no̍ a̱gne 'va̍ sṛjo a̱ghāyā̍vi̱ṣyave̍ ri̱pave̍ du̱cchunā̍yai | mā da̱tvate̱ daśa̍te̱ mādate̍ no̱ mā rīṣa̍te sahasāva̱n parā̍ dāḥ ||
english: Do not abandon us, O Agni, to the ill-intentioned foe, to the adversary or to misfortune. Do not hand us over to him who bites, who stings, who intoxicates, who harms, O powerful one.

sanskrit: vi gha̱ tvāvā̍m̐ ṛtajāta yaṁsad gṛṇā̱no a̍gne ta̱nve̱3̱̍ varū̍tham | viśvā̍d riri̱kṣor u̱ta vā̍ nini̱tsor a̍bhi̱hrutā̱m asi̱ hi de̍va vi̱ṣpaṭ ||
english: Truly one like you, O Agni born of truth, being praised, stretches out protection for his body against all who would harm or lead astray — for you, O god, are the guardian against what comes upon us crookedly.

sanskrit: tvaṁ tām̐ a̍gna u̱bhayā̱n vi vi̱dvān veṣi̍ prapi̱tve manu̍ṣo yajatra | a̱bhi̱pi̱tve mana̍ve̱ śāsyo̍ bhūr marmṛ̱jenya̍ u̱śigbhi̱r nākraḥ ||
english: O Agni, knowing both classes of mortals, you seek them both at the hour of setting forth. At the time of arrival you are to be instructed by Manu — purified and burnished by those who desire, the bird of heaven.

sanskrit: avo̍cāma ni̱vaca̍nāny asmi̱n māna̍sya sū̱nuḥ sa̍hasā̱ne a̱gnau | va̱yaṁ sa̱hasra̱m ṛṣi̍bhiḥ sanema vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: We have spoken these set hymns in this Agni of Māna's son, the powerful one. May we win a thousand with the ṛṣis — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: a̱na̱rvāṇa̍ṁ vṛṣa̱bham ma̱ndraji̍hva̱m bṛha̱spati̍ṁ vardhayā̱ navya̍m a̱rkaiḥ | gā̱thā̱nya̍ḥ su̱ruco̱ yasya̍ de̱vā ā̍śṛ̱ṇvanti̱ nava̍mānasya̱ martā̍ḥ ||
english: Increase Bṛhaspati with new hymns — he who is unopposed, vigorous, sweet-tongued. He is the singer of songs, of brilliant radiance, whose new praises the gods and mortals listen to.

sanskrit: tam ṛ̱tviyā̱ upa̱ vāca̍ḥ sacante̱ sargo̱ na yo de̍vaya̱tām asa̍rji | bṛha̱spati̱ḥ sa hy añjo̱ varā̍ṁsi̱ vibhvābha̍va̱t sam ṛ̱te mā̍ta̱riśvā̍ ||
english: The timely words attend on him, as a rush of men seeking the gods has been let loose. For Bṛhaspati straightway opened the highest realms; Mātariśvan joined together in the rite.

sanskrit: upa̍stuti̱ṁ nama̍sa̱ udya̍tiṁ ca̱ śloka̍ṁ yaṁsat savi̱teva̱ pra bā̱hū | a̱sya kratvā̍ha̱nyo̱3̱̍ yo asti̍ mṛ̱go na bhī̱mo a̍ra̱kṣasa̱s tuvi̍ṣmān ||
english: He sends forth praise and the rising of homage and sound, like Savitṛ extending his arms. By his power, the terrible one who is to be slain in battle, like a fearsome beast, without demonic protection — yet mighty.

sanskrit: a̱sya śloko̍ di̱vīya̍te pṛthi̱vyām atyo̱ na ya̍ṁsad yakṣa̱bhṛd vice̍tāḥ ||mṛ̱gāṇā̱ṁ na he̱tayo̱ yanti̍ ce̱mā bṛha̱spate̱r ahi̍māyām̐ a̱bhi dyūn ||
english: His praise flies through heaven and earth; the discerning bearer of the divine strikes like a racehorse. The arrows of the deer — these fly here; Bṛhaspati's magical powers against enemies flash toward the sky.

sanskrit: ye tvā̍ devosri̱kam manya̍mānāḥ pā̱pā bha̱dram u̍pa̱jīva̍nti pa̱jrāḥ | na dū̱ḍhye̱3̱̍ anu̍ dadāsi vā̱mam bṛha̍spate̱ caya̍sa̱ it piyā̍rum ||
english: The evil Pajras who think of you as a godless one — they wickedly live off what is good. You do not grant a boon to the deceitful one, O Bṛhaspati; you punish the despiser.

sanskrit: su̱praitu̍ḥ sū̱yava̍so̱ na panthā̍ durni̱yantu̱ḥ pari̍prīto̱ na mi̱traḥ ||a̱na̱rvāṇo̍ a̱bhi ye cakṣa̍te̱ no 'pī̍vṛtā aporṇu̱vanto̍ asthuḥ ||
english: Like a path to good pasture, easy to travel; like Mitra fully satisfied, hard to lead astray — those who are unopposed and look upon us have stood forth, opening what was veiled.

sanskrit: saṁ yaṁ stubho̱ 'vana̍yo̱ na yanti̍ samu̱draṁ na sra̱vato̱ rodha̍cakrāḥ | sa vi̱dvām̐ u̱bhaya̍ṁ caṣṭe a̱ntar bṛha̱spati̱s tara̱ āpa̍ś ca̱ gṛdhra̍ḥ ||
english: To whom praises converge like rivers flowing to the ocean with wheel-like banks — he, Bṛhaspati, the eager one, beholds both things from within: what is beyond and what are the waters.

sanskrit: e̱vā ma̱has tu̍vijā̱tas tuvi̍ṣmā̱n bṛha̱spati̍r vṛṣa̱bho dhā̍yi de̱vaḥ | sa na̍ḥ stu̱to vī̱rava̍d dhātu̱ goma̍d vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: Thus has Bṛhaspati, great, mightily born, mighty, vigorous, been placed as the divine bull. May he, when praised, grant us abundance of heroes and cattle — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

sanskrit: kaṅka̍to̱ na kaṅka̱to 'tho̍ satī̱naka̍ṅkataḥ | dvāv iti̱ pluṣī̱ iti̱ ny a1̱̍dṛṣṭā̍ alipsata ||
english: The Kaṅkata, and the one that is not Kaṅkata, and then the true Kaṅkata — saying 'two' and 'scorching,' the unseen ones have clung fast.

sanskrit: a̱dṛṣṭā̍n hanty āya̱ty atho̍ hanti parāya̱tī | atho̍ avaghna̱tī ha̱nty atho̍ pinaṣṭi piṁṣa̱tī ||
english: Coming, she slays the unseen ones; going away, she slays them too. Crushing down, she slays them; grinding, she grinds them.

sanskrit: śa̱rāsa̱ḥ kuśa̍rāso da̱rbhāsa̍ḥ sai̱ryā u̱ta | mau̱ñjā a̱dṛṣṭā̍ vairi̱ṇāḥ sarve̍ sā̱kaṁ ny a̍lipsata ||
english: Śara grasses, Kuśara grasses, Darbha grasses, and also the Sairya and Mauñja reeds — all the hostile unseen ones have together clung fast.

sanskrit: ni gāvo̍ go̱ṣṭhe a̍sada̱n ni mṛ̱gāso̍ avikṣata | ni ke̱tavo̱ janā̍nā̱ṁ ny a1̱̍dṛṣṭā̍ alipsata ||
english: The cows have settled in the cowpen; the wild animals have lain down; the banners of the peoples have been lowered — the unseen ones have clung fast.

sanskrit: e̱ta u̱ tye praty a̍dṛśran prado̱ṣaṁ taska̍rā iva | adṛ̍ṣṭā̱ viśva̍dṛṣṭā̱ḥ prati̍buddhā abhūtana ||
english: Those there have been seen at dusk, like thieves. O unseen ones, seen-by-all — you have been caught awake.

sanskrit: dyaur va̍ḥ pi̱tā pṛ̍thi̱vī mā̱tā somo̱ bhrātādi̍ti̱ḥ svasā̍ | adṛ̍ṣṭā̱ viśva̍dṛṣṭā̱s tiṣṭha̍te̱laya̍tā̱ su ka̍m ||
english: Heaven is your father, Earth your mother, Soma your brother, Aditi your sister. O unseen ones, seen-by-all — stay still and be at peace.

sanskrit: ye aṁsyā̱ ye aṅgyā̍ḥ sū̱cīkā̱ ye pra̍kaṅka̱tāḥ | adṛ̍ṣṭā̱ḥ kiṁ ca̱neha va̱ḥ sarve̍ sā̱kaṁ ni ja̍syata ||
english: Those in the shoulders, those in the limbs, those needle-like, those that are called Kaṅkata — O unseen ones, whatever you are here, all together perish.

sanskrit: ut pu̱rastā̱t sūrya̍ eti vi̱śvadṛ̍ṣṭo adṛṣṭa̱hā | a̱dṛṣṭā̱n sarvā̍ñ ja̱mbhaya̱n sarvā̍ś ca yātudhā̱nya̍ḥ ||
english: The sun rises in the east, seen by all, the slayer of the unseen. Crushing all the unseen ones and all the sorceries.

sanskrit: ud a̍paptad a̱sau sūrya̍ḥ pu̱ru viśvā̍ni̱ jūrva̍n | ā̱di̱tyaḥ parva̍tebhyo vi̱śvadṛ̍ṣṭo adṛṣṭa̱hā ||
english: That sun has flown up, consuming all the many things; the Āditya from the mountains, seen by all, the slayer of the unseen.

sanskrit: sūrye̍ vi̱ṣam ā sa̍jāmi̱ dṛti̱ṁ surā̍vato gṛ̱he | so ci̱n nu na ma̍rāti̱ no va̱yam ma̍rāmā̱re a̍sya̱ yoja̍naṁ hari̱ṣṭhā madhu̍ tvā madhu̱lā ca̍kāra ||
english: I fasten the poison to the sun, to the leather flask in the house of the soma-presser. It shall not now die, nor shall we die — far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.

sanskrit: i̱ya̱tti̱kā śa̍kunti̱kā sa̱kā ja̍ghāsa te vi̱ṣam | so ci̱n nu na ma̍rāti̱ no va̱yam ma̍rāmā̱re a̍sya̱ yoja̍naṁ hari̱ṣṭhā madhu̍ tvā madhu̱lā ca̍kāra ||
english: The little iyattika bird, together with the śakuntikā bird, has eaten your poison. It shall not now die, nor shall we die — far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.

sanskrit: triḥ sa̱pta vi̍ṣpuliṅga̱kā vi̱ṣasya̱ puṣya̍m akṣan | tāś ci̱n nu na ma̍ranti̱ no va̱yam ma̍rāmā̱re a̍sya̱ yoja̍naṁ hari̱ṣṭhā madhu̍ tvā madhu̱lā ca̍kāra ||
english: Thrice seven viṣpuliṅkā birds have sucked up the flower of the poison. They shall not now die, nor shall we die — far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.

sanskrit: na̱vā̱nāṁ na̍vatī̱nāṁ vi̱ṣasya̱ ropu̍ṣīṇām | sarvā̍sām agrabha̱ṁ nāmā̱re a̍sya̱ yoja̍naṁ hari̱ṣṭhā madhu̍ tvā madhu̱lā ca̍kāra ||
english: Of the nine, and of the ninety, of the festering poisons — I have seized the names of all of them. Far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.

sanskrit: triḥ sa̱pta ma̍yū̱rya̍ḥ sa̱pta svasā̍ro a̱gruva̍ḥ | tās te̍ vi̱ṣaṁ vi ja̍bhrira uda̱kaṁ ku̱mbhinī̍r iva ||
english: Thrice seven peahens, the seven unmarried sisters — they have carried off your poison like water-carrying women carrying pots.

sanskrit: i̱ya̱tta̱kaḥ ku̍ṣumbha̱kas ta̱kam bhi̍na̱dmy aśma̍nā | tato̍ vi̱ṣam pra vā̍vṛte̱ parā̍cī̱r anu̍ sa̱ṁvata̍ḥ ||
english: This little kuṣumbhaka — I split open the taka with a stone. From it the poison has flowed back, flowing away along the valleys.

sanskrit: ku̱ṣu̱mbha̱kas tad a̍bravīd gi̱reḥ pra̍vartamāna̱kaḥ | vṛści̍kasyāra̱saṁ vi̱ṣam a̍ra̱saṁ vṛ̍ścika te vi̱ṣam ||
english: The kuṣumbhaka, rolling down from the mountain, declared: 'The poison of the scorpion is without power — without power is your poison, O scorpion.'
